title: Ahi, che male!
summary: Body vocab and the mi fa male / mi fanno male agreement pattern

blocks.title: Quando qualcosa fa male
blocks.body: To say something hurts, Italian uses **fare** the way English uses 'hurt': *mi fa male la testa* (my head hurts) — literally 'to me it makes pain, the head.' Same trap as *piacere*: the verb agrees with **what hurts**, not with you. One thing hurting → **fa**. More than one → **fanno**: *mi fanno male i piedi* (my feet hurt).
blocks.callout: Same shape as mi piace / mi piacciono — the verb agrees with the thing, always.

blocks.title: Fa o fanno? Conta quante cose fanno male

pairs.left: *Mi fa male la testa.* — My head hurts. (one thing: la testa)
pairs.right: *Mi fanno male i piedi.* — My feet hurt. (more than one: i piedi)
pairs.note: Singular subject → fa. Plural subject → fanno. The subject is what hurts, not you.
Same pattern with any body part — check singular vs plural before picking fa/fanno.

blocks.prompt: You've been walking all day. Your feet hurt. Which is correct?
blocks.explain: *i piedi* is plural, so the verb has to be plural too: *mi fanno male i piedi*.

blocks.hint: la schiena is singular — fa, not fanno.
blocks.explain: *Mi fa male la schiena* — singular subject, singular verb.

blocks.title: Ancora parti del corpo
blocks.body: A few more useful ones: *la mano* (hand — feminine, even though it ends in -o) and its plural *le mani*; *l'occhio / gli occhi* (eye/eyes); *il dente / i denti* (tooth/teeth); *il naso* (nose — you've only got one). *la mano* is the classic exception every beginner trips on.
blocks.callout: la mano is feminine — un'eccezione da ricordare.

blocks.title: Cosa ti fa male?
blocks.prompt: Build a sentence about what hurts, and when.
blocks.sample: Dopo la palestra, mi fanno male le gambe.

blocks.prompt: Cosa ti fa male oggi, o questa settimana? Scrivi 2–3 frasi con mi fa male / mi fanno male.
